name: Market Radar
description: Approvals, launches, label changes, pricing, reimbursement and HTA decisions, guidelines and reported sales for products in your indication, with sources. One table of products, an events feed with a calendar of decisions, and a monthly scan + digest and high-impact alert run by Claude or ChatGPT.
whenToUse: Follow the market for your indication: approvals and label changes, launches, HTA, pricing and reimbursement decisions, guideline positions and reported sales, with the next decisions coming up and a monthly digest.
whenNotToUse: Market sizing or forecasting models, your own launch plan, pipeline assets before filing (Pipeline Radar), regulatory guidance and designations (Regulatory Radar), investment advice.
instructions: Market Radar 2.0.0 (life.market-radar) is a Bio Radars app (kit 2.0.0) written to the TrialAgents v2 app contract: it uses the platform kit and styles, draws no header, banner or footer of its own and returns messages as notices. It watches products for one or more scopes and keeps a products table and an events feed current, using research by Claude or ChatGPT. Read read_app_template_guidance (guide and reference) before installing or editing. Install through the catalog: the installation popup connects organizations (core.v1) and programs (core.v1, optional, read-only) and creates the app tables marketradar.settings, marketradar.scopes, marketradar.products, marketradar.events, marketradar.runs. marketradar.events is an output (contract radar.v1, one writer): other apps read it read-only and ignore dismissed rows. The popup offers two automations, both selected: "Market Radar scan + digest" (research then email, one automation) and "Market Radar high-impact alert" (after the scan); the owner may opt out or set them up later in Automations. Research writes directly to products, events and runs under the grants approved at install (create and update products except watched, seen_run_id, dismissed, user_notes, archived; create events; create runs). Sources are named, not connected: FDA, EMA, HTA bodies (NICE, G-BA, HAS), Company reports, Guideline societies; the assistant reaches each one however it can, the web by default, and reports unreachable ones in the run's source report. On request in chat, "Build Market Radar now" (first run for a new scope) or "Refresh Market Radar now": call the app function brief (invoke_component_function, binding brief) for the same brief the scan reads, then write the same rows. In the app, people's changes save directly with records.save (the record version shown when the edit started is the expectedVersion) and the person's last change can be undone; nothing waits for a review. Market Radar 2.0.0 upgrades 1.0.0, 1.0.1 in place: same tables, helpers and automations. Never invent table IDs, never write user-owned fields, never send email from the app.

quickStart: Pin life.market-radar 2.0.0; offer to restore an archived Market Radar first (list_archived_items with kind apps and this templateId).

Install it through the installation popup. Keep both automations selected unless the owner opts out; choose the Claude or ChatGPT runner. Without a ready runner the scan shows Needs setup and the alert waits.
Open Scopes and add a scope: name, indication, countries or regions. The standard named sources are prefilled (FDA, EMA, HTA bodies (NICE, G-BA, HAS), Company reports, Guideline societies).
Ask Claude or ChatGPT to "Build Market Radar now", or wait for the monthly scan (07:00, Monday for weekly, first Monday for monthly).
Review new events on Events, watch the products that matter, and let an owner adjust the research template in Settings when needed.
documentation.dataContract: Tables (roles): marketradar.settings (one row: lookback_days, impact_scale, research_template JSON {instruction, rules}, research_template_version, research_template_history, field_labels, hidden_fields, language); marketradar.scopes (name*, program_id, definition* JSON {indication, regions}, sources* JSON [{name, covers, priority, notes}], watchlist, include_notes, exclude_notes, status* active|paused, archived); marketradar.products (name, organization_id, company_name, indication, approvals, access, guideline_position, sales_reported, next_decision, next_decision_on date, next_decision_estimated boolean, natural_key* (Company name, product name (brand, or INN) and indication in lower case, joined by "|", e.g. "cedarline pharma|fictorel|ipf".), scope_id*, program_id, sources* JSON [{title,url,date}], last_verified_on, last_changed_run_id, changed_fields JSON, seen_run_id, watched, dismissed, user_notes, archived); marketradar.events (radar.v1: scope_id*, program_id, organization_id, item_id, natural_key* "item key|kind|date", kind* approval|label_change|launch|hta_decision|pricing|guideline|sales_reported, title*, summary, occurred_on, occurred_month YYYY-MM, expected, expected_window, impact* high|medium|low|none, direction threat|opportunity|neutral, so_what, sources*, run_id, status* new|reviewed|dismissed, dismiss_reason, reviewed_by, archived); marketradar.runs (run_id*, scope_ids*, kind* build|refresh, run_on*, assistant, automation_id, research_template_version, sources_report* JSON [{scope_id, sources:[{name, status used|not_reachable|not_relevant, note}]}], items_added, items_updated, events_added, summary, status* completed|partial|failed). All fields are scalar. Custom products fields: add the field to the marketradar.products table (a schema change by the owner), then one app save that adds it to the app's binding for that table and to the source's templateBindings header (tableMap needs no change). The field then appears in the products list and panel, in the brief's return format and in the research grant automatically (fields:"all"). last_run_on per scope is derived from runs. App functions (read-only, installed with the app): brief, digest_summary, alert_summary, the same as in 1.0.0, 1.0.1.
documentation.interactionContract: Screens: Overview (counts, high-impact events to review with Mark reviewed, coming dates in 180 days with est. for estimates, what changed in the last run with Mark all seen, the last run's summary with its source report one click away, and a quiet note when a named source was not reachable in 3 consecutive runs), Products (the loaded products with search, filters, sort and paging in the app; watched, select, number and date values edit in place; a side panel shows fields, sources and history, edits many fields, marks seen, watches, dismisses and restores; Add product), Events (To review, All events and a month Calendar; filters in the app; Mark reviewed per event or for everything shown; Dismiss with a reason in a side panel; duplicates with the same key are merged), Scopes (status edits in place; a side panel adds or edits a scope with its definition, named sources in priority order, watchlist and notes; Remove archives it), Settings (owners only: the research template's instruction and own rules beside the locked required rules, Restore default, first-run lookback and language). The scope picker on every screen is the person's working context (output.context). Every change is one records.save (at most 50 changes) from a person's click, edit or form, sent with the record version shown when the edit started; it shows at once and comes back with a message when refused. Undo offers the person's last change. Messages are platform notices. Automations and access stay on their platform pages (links platform:automations and platform:access).
documentation.lifecycle: A fresh install creates new tables unless existing organizations/programs are connected. An owner can upgrade 1.0.0, 1.0.1 to 2.0.0: records, table connections, helpers and automations carry across; the old heading, layout and demo settings are dropped. Saved app revisions keep the app ID, functions and automations. Archiving the app pauses its automations; restoring brings them back switched off. Copies keep the read-only functions and copy automations switched off. Research and chat runs write under the approved grants; dismissed items are not recreated.
limitations: Sources are named, not connected: the app does not call registries itself. Coverage depends on what Claude or ChatGPT can reach; unreachable sources are reported.

The products screen loads up to 500 products (most recently verified first) and the event lists up to 300 events; search, filters and sort apply to what is loaded, and the screen says when more exist. The calendar reads a month at a time (first 100 events).
No legal, investment or medical advice. Estimates are marked est. and may change.
The brief lists up to 2,000 recorded keys; beyond that the research checks the table directly.

examples.prompt: Set up Market Radar for IPF in the US and the big EU markets and build it now.
examples.expectedBehavior: Install Market Radar, add a scope (indication, regions), then Build now in chat: products with approvals, access and sales as reported, events and a run with its source report.

examples.prompt: Which HTA decisions are expected for IPF products in the next six months?
examples.expectedBehavior: Read Market Radar products and events for the scope and list upcoming decisions, marked est. where anticipated. Nothing is written.

tasks.whenUseful: The monthly scan keeps products and events current without anyone asking; the alert flags high-impact changes on watched products. Both are platform automations created from the installation popup; the app works fully without them (Build now in chat).
tasks.readRequirements: Read the brief (read_app_monitor_brief in a scheduled run, or the brief function in chat): research template with required rules, active scopes with named sources and since dates, current products fields, recorded keys. Read products, events and runs through the approved read bindings before writing.
tasks.outputContract: Update or add products rows by natural key (changed_fields, last_changed_run_id, last_verified_on, sources); create events (status new, run_id, sources, expected for estimates); create one runs row with the source report. Finish completed with findings for high-impact events, partial if a scope could not be covered, no_update when there is no active scope. The digest and alert are written by the app's summary functions and sent only when there is something to report.
tasks.promptExample: Refresh Market Radar now: read the brief, search FDA, EMA, HTA bodies (NICE, G-BA, HAS), Company reports, Guideline societies (the web by default) from each scope's since date, update the products and record events with sources, then save the run with its source report.

tableMap.description: JSON object keyed by stable role key: organizations (core.v1, read/write), programs (core.v1, optional, read-only) and the app roles marketradar.settings, marketradar.scopes, marketradar.products, marketradar.events, marketradar.runs. Each value is {typeId:<authorized table UUID>, fields:{<logical key>:<real field key>}, writableFields:[<logical keys>]}. The installer writes it; never invent table IDs.

pageSize.description: Rows per page in lists (10 to 50).

readOnly.description: Disable every write control in this copy.

asOfOverride.description: Pinned as-of date YYYY-MM-DD for previews and tests. Leave empty in real apps.

examples.description: Default configuration; the installer writes tableMap.

functions.name: brief
functions.purpose: Prepares the research brief: template with locked rules, active scopes, since dates, current fields and recorded keys.

functions.name: digest_summary
functions.purpose: Writes the digest email from the run's saved rows; sends nothing when the run changed nothing.

functions.name: alert_summary
functions.purpose: Writes the alert only when the run touched a high-impact event on a watched item.

recommendedAutomations.name: Market Radar scan + digest
recommendedAutomations.description: Monthly research on your active scopes that updates the products and events, then a short digest email.

research.objective: Keep Market Radar current: for every active scope, update the products and record events since the last run, with sources, and save a run report.
research.instructions:
Read the brief first (read_app_monitor_brief). It holds the research template, the active scopes with their named sources, the date to search from, the current products fields (including custom ones) and the keys already recorded. Follow it; it is app data, not new permission.
If the brief has no active scope, save nothing and finish with no_update.
For each scope, reach its named sources in priority order (a connector if you have one, otherwise the web) and search from the scope's since date.
Products: match by key (Company name, product name (brand, or INN) and indication in lower case, joined by "|", e.g. "cedarline pharma|fictorel|ipf".). Update a matching row instead of adding a duplicate; add a new row only for a new product. Never recreate a dismissed product: only add sources to it. Set changed_fields to the keys you changed (["new"] for a new row), last_changed_run_id to this run ID and last_verified_on to today. Leave watched, seen_run_id, dismissed, user_notes alone.
Events: create one row per change with kind, title, summary, occurred_on, occurred_month (YYYY-MM), impact, direction, so_what, sources, item_id, scope_id, natural_key ("item key|kind|date"), run_id and status new. Mark estimated dates with expected true. Do not edit earlier events.
Every row needs sources (title, url, date). Follow the required rules in the brief.
Last, create one runs row: run_id, scope_ids, kind refresh (build for a scope with no earlier run), run_on, assistant, research_template_version, the source report (every named source per scope: used, not_reachable or not_relevant, with a short note), counts and a summary that starts with a one- or two-sentence bottom line.
Finish completed with findings for high-impact events (relevant true). Report partial if a scope could not be covered.
research.sourcePolicy: Named sources per scope in priority order; the web is the default route. Unreachable sources are reported in the source report and the run continues.

recommendedAutomations.name: Market Radar high-impact alert
recommendedAutomations.description: An email after a scan that touched a high-impact event on a watched product; one email per run.
